stories.title: Iranian singer lashed 74 times for performing without hijab after conviction for ‘outraging public decency’
stories.dek: Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, was lashed on Monday over the live-streamed YouTube concert in 2024, which went viral in Iran.
stories.content:
An Iranian singer was lashed 74 times after being convicted of “outraging public decency” over a performance in which she performed without her hijab.

Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, was whipped on Monday over the livestreamed YouTube concert in 2024, which went viral in Iran.

In Iran, women are banned from singing by themselves in public and are required by law to wear a hijab and modest clothes in public.

The concert was filmed at the Dayr-Gachin Caravanserai, a historic site along the Silk Road route in Iran, on Dec. 11, 2024. There was no live audience, but the video was viewed around 3 million times.

Ahmadi wore a sleeveless dress and no headscarf during the performance.

In the description of the concert, shared on her YouTube channel, Ahmadi wrote: “I want to sing for the people I love. This is a right that I could not give up, that is, singing for the land that I love passionately.”

In June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of “offending public decency by producing and disseminating vulgar and immoral content online.”

The artist’s lawyers appealed the sentence in September, but it was rejected.

Artists Sohail Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri and Amirali Pirnia, who also performed, and concert organizer Mohsen Lashkari, were also lashed, EuroNews reported.

In addition to the flogging, all five artists were sentenced to a two-year travel ban and a two-year ban on artistic activity.

Ahmadi’s lawyer told Iranian newspaper Etemad that Ahmadi and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in Qom on Monday for their punishments.

stories.title: Israel seeks to jail Palestinian student activist without trial after dorm arrest
stories.dek: Mahdi Tounsi appeared with visible bruising after being interrogated by police on his association with Israeli-Palestinian organisations Israeli professors, students and rights activists are calling f…
stories.content:
Detained student Mahdi Tounsi with his cats. His hair and beard were shaved in detention, and his glasses were taken away. Photograph: Handout View image in fullscreen Detained student Mahdi Tounsi with his cats. His hair and beard were shaved in detention, and his glasses were taken away. Photograph: Handout Israel Israel seeks to jail Palestinian student activist without trial after dorm arrest Mahdi Tounsi appeared with visible bruising after being interrogated by police on his association with Israeli-Palestinian organisations

Israeli professors, students and rights activists are calling for the immediate release of Mahdi Tounsi, a sociology student at Jerusalem’s Hebrew University who has been held without charge for more than two weeks after he was seized from his dorm room.

The detention comes amid a racist campaign of delegitimisation against Palestinian citizens of Israel, whose votes were critical to stripping Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition of its majority in elections last month.

Police took Tounsi, 26, a criminology and sociology student from East Jerusalem who is active in Jewish-Palestinian campaign groups, from his dorm room on 8 November.

When he appeared by video link at a court hearing on 19 November he had visible bruises on his face, did not have the glasses he needs to see properly, and his hair and beard had been shaved.

Tounsi told his lawyer that police beat him in the dorm, in the patrol car and at the police station, Israeli media reported . Interrogators questioned him about his activism with Israeli-Palestinian organisations Standing Together and Ir Amim.

Both groups called for his immediate release and warned against using security agencies to silence political activity and critical speech.

“[This] could happen to any student and any one of us, especially in a month when the government is persecuting Arab citizens, from [ journalist ] Abed Abu Shehadeh to the leaders of Arab political parties,” Standing Together said in a statement, calling on the university to intervene to ensure a fair judicial process.

View image in fullscreen A screengrab of Mahdi Tounsi in custody. Photograph: Ofer Cassif/X Ir Amim described Tounsi as thoughtful, gentle and a valued partner “in movements bringing Palestinians and Israelis together”, in a statement that also warned of “serious concerns for his safety, wellbeing, and right to due process”.

After losing the election, Netanyahu and his allies weaponised false accusations of mass fraud – Israel’s election commission validated the results – in an attempt to hold on to power by delegitimising the votes of Palestinian citizens of Israel.

stories.title: Iranian singer subjected to 74 lashes for performing without her hijab
stories.dek: An Iranian singer and four members of her production team have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for "offending public decency ‌by producing and publishing obscene and immoral content onli…
stories.content:
People walk past a mural depicting the late leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, and Iran's late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, on a street in Tehran on Nov. 20. (Majid Asgaripour/West Asia News Agency/Reuters) Social Sharing An Iranian singer and four members of her production team have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for "offending public decency ‌by producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online," an Iranian news website said on Monday.

Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others ​were also handed two-year bans on artistic ​and musical activities and travel, the Emtedad website quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili as saying.

The ​case followed the release of a ⁠video on YouTube ⁠in December 2024 showing ‌Ahmadi performing without the mandatory hijab alongside male musicians in Qom, south of the capital of Tehran, Norway-based human rights group Hengaw said.

Western governments ⁠and human rights groups have criticized flogging as torture and a violation of international law. Iran rejects accusations ‌over its human rights record, saying Western countries should focus on their own human rights problems.

Iranian authorities did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment by Reuters.

A woman holds a placard with a picture of Iranian woman Mahsa Amini during a protest against her death, in Berlin, Sept. 28, 2022. (Markus Schreiber/The Associated Press)

Rules requiring women to wear the ⁠hijab were a flashpoint during protests in 2022 after ⁠the in-custody death of Kurdish Iranian woman Mahsa ⁠Amini, ⁠who was ​arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.

The rules have increasingly ​been flouted on ⁠the streets of Tehran and beyond, and enforcement of the rules has also become more selective.

Emtedad did not specify whether Nili had represented the five defendants.

stories.title: Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
stories.dek: Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail.
stories.content:
Kagi Mail is launching in public beta with a 60-day free trial.

Kagi Mail is launching in public beta with a 60-day free trial.

Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.”

With Kagi Mail, you get an @ kagimail.com address, but the service also supports unlimited aliases and domains. It also offers 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. On the roadmap, you can expect contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, but native mobile apps aren’t expected to arrive until Q3 2027.

“Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once,” Kagi says. “There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way.”

Kagi Mail is available now with a 60-day free trial before you have to pay $99 per year. The service is available as part of a $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription.

stories.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
stories.dek: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it.
stories.content:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.

The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.

The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics , demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.

In everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.

In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.

Quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.

The prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.

Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.

These theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly important in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.

stories.source: Crisis Group & Diplomatic Reviews • 6 min read
stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
papers.tldr: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins.
takeaways: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies.
We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences.

We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU.

papers.title: The resource--invariant gap: a protected Floquet invariant need not protect Wigner negativity
papers.authors: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorwé, Nsangou Mama et al.
papers.tldr: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open. We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss.
takeaways: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open.
We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss.

The quasienergy windings remain quantized at every chain length, yet the matched sector contrast flips sign when the chain grows under index-end shielding and is null within $3\times 10^{-5}$ under uniform loss at $t=T$ for $d\le 0.5$.

papers.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Chenyang Liao, Chihang Luo, Xin Chen et al.
papers.tldr: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices.
takeaways: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility.
Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), successfully demonstrating external nanoscale nuclear-spin detection.
These results establish our SiC nanopillars as robust building blocks for scanning quantum probes and scalable sensor networks.

papers.title: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir
papers.tldr: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts.
takeaways: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout.
We do not find a clear systematic dependence of limit-cycle persistence on coherence across the reservoir ensemble.
We conclude that, within this simulated reservoir, the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.

papers.title: Spin dynamics in disordered systems with generic spin-momentum couplings: A matrix-rational formulation
papers.tldr: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings. Starting from the Diffuson, we introduce a matrix-valued rational approximation for its frequency dependence that does not rely on a low-frequency or weak-coupling expansion.
takeaways: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings.

Comparisons with direct numerical simulations demonstrate quantitative agreement for both the post-quench spin dynamics and spin relaxation times across a broad range of coupling strengths, extending beyond the diffusive regime.
The matrix-rational formulation provides a unified description of ultrafast spin dynamics and long-time relaxation.
